evidence.quote: (The earlier bankroll figure didn't reflect the flop bet, so I've corrected it here.)

criteria.why: Turn 4 talks about its own correction instead of staying in dealer voice. The other replies are plain dealer talk.

evidence.quote: You bet the pot (20) and the dealer calls, so the pot is now 60.
The river is the 6♥, and you checked.

criteria.why: Most moves are answered. In turn 4 the reply re-narrates the river and the check instead of acting on a fresh move. In turn 3 the river came with no showdown, and turn 4 then reran the river.

evidence.quote: The dealer's 4♠ and 5♦ make a six-high straight with the 2♣, 3♦ and 6♥, which beats your A-high. The dealer takes the 60 pot.

criteria.why: The dealer plays out and settles the hand itself and never hands a house job to the player. The one slip is that turn 3 stalled at the river instead of going to showdown.

evidence.quote: Your bankroll is now 960: the 10 blind and the 20 flop bet are gone.
You lose 30 on this hand (10 blind and 20 on the flop).
the dealer takes the 20 pot. You lose only the 10 big blind you'd already posted, and your bankroll stays at 960.

criteria.why: Bankroll and pot figures contradict earlier turns. The bankroll stayed 990 while the pot reached 60, and the 60 pot would mean a 30 loss, so 960 fits only by coincidence. Turn 6 says you lose 10 yet leaves the bankroll at 960, and turn 8 shows a 60 pot while the bankroll stays 960. The turn 4 note admits the earlier figures were wrong.
